questions.question: If sin A - cos A = \(\frac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{2}\) , then the value of sin A. cos A is:
questions.questionHtml: If sin A - cos A = \(\frac{\sqrt{3} - \sqrt{2}}{2}\), then the value of sin A. cos A is:
questions.solution:
sin A - cos A = (√3 - √2)/2 ⇒ (sin A - cos A)2 = [(√3 - √2)/2]2 = (5 - 2√6)/4

1 - 2 sin A cos A = (5 - 2√6)/4 ⇒ -2 sin A cos A = (1 - 2√6)/4 - 1

-2 sin A cos A = (1 - 2√6 - 4)/4 ⇒ sin A cos A = (2√6 - 1)/8

questions.question: The following bar chart shows the year-wise percentage hike in the fuel price with respect to the previous year. In how many years did the fuel prices NOT rise?
questions.questionHtml:
The following bar chart shows the year-wise percentage hike in the fuel price with respect to the previous year.

In how many years did the fuel prices NOT rise?
questions.solution:
Given:

The bar chart shows the year-wise percentage hike in fuel prices for the years 2015 to 2021.

We need to determine how many years the fuel prices did not rise (fuel price hike = 0%).

Formula used:

If fuel price hike (%) = 0, it indicates no rise in fuel prices for that year.

Calculations:

From the chart:

1. In 2015: Fuel price hike = 8% (prices rose).

2. In 2016: Fuel price hike = 10.5% (prices rose).

3. In 2017: Fuel price hike = 6% (prices rose).

4. In 2018: Fuel price hike = 7% (prices rose).

5. In 2019: Fuel price hike = 8% (prices rose).

6. In 2020: Fuel price hike = 10% (prices rose).

7. In 2021: Fuel price hike = 11% (prices rose).

Observation: In all years from 2015 to 2021, the fuel price hike was greater than 0%.

∴ The number of years the fuel prices did NOT rise is 0.

questions.question: The least number which must be subtracted from 7278745 so as to obtain a sum that is divisible by 11 is:
questions.questionHtml: The least number which must be subtracted from 7278745 so as to obtain a sum that is divisible by 11 is:
questions.solution:
Sum of odd position digits: 7 + 7 + 7 + 5 = 26

Sum of even position digits: 2 + 8 + 4 = 14

Difference: 26 - 14 = 12

Least subtraction: 12 - 11 = 1

questions.question: A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/h in still water goes 50 km downstream and comes back in a total of 7 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:
questions.questionHtml: A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/h in still water goes 50 km downstream and comes back in a total of 7 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:
questions.solution:
Let speed of stream = x km/h.

Downstream speed = (15 + x), Upstream speed = (15 - x)

Total time: \(\frac{50}{15+x} + \frac{50}{15-x} = 7.5\)

LCM: 50(15 - x) + 50(15 + x) = 7.5(225 - x2)

1500 = 7.5(225 - x²) ⇒ x² = 25 ⇒ x = 5

Speed of the stream = 5 km/h.

questions.question: The length, breadth and height of a room is 15 m, 9 m, and 5 m, respectively. From each can of paint 40 square metre of area is painted. How many cans of paint will be needed to paint only the walls of the room?
questions.questionHtml: The length, breadth and height of a room is 15 m, 9 m, and 5 m, respectively. From each can of paint 40 square metre of area is painted. How many cans of paint will be needed to paint only the walls of the room?
questions.solution:
Area of four walls = 2h(l + b) = 2 × 5(15 + 9) = 2 × 5 × 24 = 240 m²

Cans needed = 240 / 40 = 6

questions.question: The marked price of 55 items was equal to the cost price of 99 items. The selling price of 56 items was equal to the marked price of 35 items. Calculate the profit or loss percentage from the sale of each item.
questions.questionHtml: The marked price of 55 items was equal to the cost price of 99 items. The selling price of 56 items was equal to the marked price of 35 items. Calculate the profit or loss percentage from the sale of each item.
questions.solution:
55 MP = 99 CP ⇒ MP = 9/5 CP

56 SP = 35 MP ⇒ SP = 5/8 MP

SP = 5/8 × 9/5 CP = 9/8 CP,

Profit% = (9/8 CP - CP)/CP × 100 = 1/8 × 100 = 12.5%

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, P received 42% of the valid votes and Q won by 45,360 votes. 20% people did not cast their vote. If 10% of the votes cast were found invalid, what is the total number of votes registered in the poll booth?
questions.questionHtml: In an election between two candidates, P received 42% of the valid votes and Q won by 45,360 votes. 20% people did not cast their vote. If 10% of the votes cast were found invalid, what is the total number of votes registered in the poll booth?
questions.solution:
P's votes = 42% of 72% of V , Q's votes = 58% of 72% of V

Difference = 16% of 72% of V = 45,360 ⇒ 0.16 × 0.72 × V = 45,360

V = 45,360 / 0.1152 = 3,93,750

questions.question: Hema is 20 years old and her sister Neha is 30 years old. How many years ago were their ages in the ratio of 3 : 5?
questions.questionHtml: Hema is 20 years old and her sister Neha is 30 years old. How many years ago were their ages in the ratio of 3 : 5?
questions.solution:
Let the number of years ago be x.

(20 - x)/(30 - x) = 3/5 ⇒ 5(20 - x) = 3(30 - x) ⇒ 100 - 5x = 90 - 3x,

10 = 2x ⇒ x = 5

questions.question: AB is the chord of the circle with centre O. A line segment DOC originating from a point D on the circumference of the circle in major segment meets AB produced at C such that BC = OD. If angle BCO = 30º, then angle AOD is:
questions.questionHtml: AB is the chord of the circle with centre O. A line segment DOC originating from a point D on the circumference of the circle in major segment meets AB produced at C such that BC = OD. If angle BCO = 30º, then angle AOD is:
questions.solution:
In ΔBOC, ∠BCO = ∠BOC = 30º ⇒ ∠OBC = 180º - 30º - 30º = 120º 

In ΔOBA, ∠OBA = ∠OAB = 180º - 120º = 60º ⇒ ∠AOB = 180º - 60º - 60º = 60º

∠AOD = 180º - 60º - 30º = 90º

questions.question: The following pie chart shows the percentage distribution of the expenditure incurred in publishing a book. Study the pie chart and answer the question that follows. If the expenditure on royalty in publishing certain number of books be ₹43,500, then what is the combined expenditure (in ₹) on transportation, binding and printing?
questions.questionHtml:
The following pie chart shows the percentage distribution of the expenditure incurred in publishing a book. Study the pie chart and answer the question that follows.

If the expenditure on royalty in publishing certain number of books be ₹43,500, then what is the combined expenditure (in ₹) on transportation, binding and printing?
questions.solution:
Total expenditure = (43,500 / 15) × 100 = ₹2,90,000

Transportation = (10 / 100) × 2,90,000 = ₹29,000

Binding = (16 / 100) × 2,90,000 = ₹46,400

Printing = (25 / 100) × 2,90,000 = ₹72,500

Combined expenditure = 29,000 + 46,400 + 72,500 = ₹1,47,900

questions.question: The given pie-chart shows the percentage distribution of the expenditure incurred in publishing a book. What is the central angle of the sector corresponding to the expenditure incurred on binding?

The given pie-chart shows the percentage distribution of the expenditure incurred in publishing a book.

What is the central angle of the sector corresponding to the expenditure incurred on binding?
questions.solution:
Given:

Percentage of expenditure on binding = 23%

We need to calculate the central angle of the sector corresponding to binding.

Formula used:

Central angle = (Percentage / 100) × 360°

Calculations:

Central angle for binding:

⇒ Central angle = (23 / 100) × 360°

⇒ Central angle = 82.8°

∴ The central angle corresponding to the expenditure on binding is 82.8°.

questions.solution:
XA = 18 cm, XB = 18 + 22 = 40 cm

18 × 40 = 24 × XD ⇒ XD = 720 / 24 = 30 cm

questions.question: Study the below table and answer the question that follows. Day of the week Distance jogged (in km) Monday 6 Tuesday 5.5 Wednesday 5.5 Thursday 7 Friday 5 Saturday 3.5 Sunday 7.5 If 300 calories are burned by jogging 6 km, then how many calories were burnt in the given week?
questions.questionHtml:
Study the below table and answer the question that follows.
Day of the week Distance jogged (in km)
Monday 6
Tuesday 5.5
Wednesday 5.5
Thursday 7
Friday 5
Saturday 3.5
Sunday 7.5

If 300 calories are burned by jogging 6 km, then how many calories were burnt in the given week?
questions.solution:
Formula used:

Calories burned = (Distance jogged / 6) × 300

Calculations:

Total distance jogged in the week:

⇒ Total distance = 6 + 5.5 + 5.5 + 7 + 5 + 3.5 + 7.5 = 40 km

Total calories burned:

⇒ Calories burned = (40 / 6) × 300

⇒ Calories burned = 2000

∴ The total calories burned in the given week is 2000 calories.

questions.question: If cos A + cos 2 A = 1 then sin 2 A + sin 4 A is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If cos A + cos2A = 1 then sin2A + sin4A is equal to:
questions.solution:
cos A + cos 2A = 1 ⇒ cos 2A = 1 - cos A

sin 2A = cos A ⇒ sin 4A = (cos A)2

sin 2A + sin 4A = cos A + (cos A)2 = 1

questions.question: The value of : \(\frac{1}{cosec \theta - \cot \theta} - \frac{1}{\sin \theta}\) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The value of : \(\frac{1}{cosec \theta - \cot \theta} - \frac{1}{\sin \theta}\) is equal to:
questions.solution:
\(\frac{1}{\csc \theta - \cot \theta} - \frac{1}{\sin \theta} \) ⇒ \( \frac{1}{\frac{1 - \cos \theta}{\sin \theta}} - \frac{1}{\sin \theta} \) ⇒ \(\frac{\sin \theta}{1 - \cos \theta} - \frac{1}{\sin \theta} \)

\(\frac{\sin^2 \theta - (1 - \cos \theta)}{(1 - \cos \theta)\sin \theta} \) ⇒ \( \frac{-\cos \theta}{\sin \theta} = -\cot \theta \)

questions.question: Ten chairs and six tables together cost ₹5,140; three chairs and two tables together cost ₹1,635. The cost of 1 chair and 1 table is:
questions.questionHtml: Ten chairs and six tables together cost ₹5,140; three chairs and two tables together cost ₹1,635. The cost of 1 chair and 1 table is:
questions.solution:
10x + 6y = 5140 , 3x + 2y = 1635

Multiply second equation by 3: 9x + 6y = 4905 , Subtract from first: x = 235

Substitute x in second: 705 + 2y = 1635 ⇒ y = 465

x + y = 235 + 465 = 700

questions.question: If a + b + c = 0, then the value of (a 2 + b 2 + 2ab) is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: If a + b + c = 0, then the value of (a<sup>2</sup> + b<sup>2</sup> + 2ab) is equal to:
questions.solution:
a + b + c = 0 ⇒ c = -(a + b)

(a2 + b2 + 2ab) = (a + b)2 ⇒ (a + b)2 = (-c)2 = c2

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum for 8 years is three-fifth of the sum. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.questionHtml: The simple interest on a sum for 8 years is three-fifth of the sum. The rate of interest per annum is:
questions.solution:
SI for 8 years = (3/5)P SI = P × R × 8/100

(3/5)P = P × R × 8/100 ⇒ (3/5) = R × 8/100

R = (3/5) × (100/8) = 300/40 = 7.5%

questions.question: A mango juice is made by mixing water and mango concentrate in the ratio 9 : 7. If x litres of water and 3x litres of mango concentrate is mixed in 160 litres of mango juice, then the new ratio becomes 13 : 14. What is the quantity of the new mango juice (in litres)?
questions.questionHtml: A mango juice is made by mixing water and mango concentrate in the ratio 9 : 7. If x litres of water and 3x litres of mango concentrate is mixed in 160 litres of mango juice, then the new ratio becomes 13 : 14. What is the quantity of the new mango juice (in litres)?
questions.solution:
Initial quantities: Water = (9/16) × 160 = 90 litres, Mango concentrate = (7/16) × 160 = 70 litres

New quantities: Water = 90 + x, Mango concentrate = 70 + 3x

New ratio: (90 + x)/(70 + 3x) = 13/14, 14(90 + x) = 13(70 + 3x)

Solving for x: 14x - 13(3x) = 910 - 1260, x = 14

Total quantity: 160 + x + 3x = 216 litres

questions.question: Three pipes, P, Q and R, together take four hours to fill a tank. All the three pipes were opened at the same time. After three hours, P was closed, and Q and R filled the remaining tank in two hours. How many hours will P alone take to fill the tank?
questions.questionHtml: Three pipes, P, Q and R, together take four hours to fill a tank. All the three pipes were opened at the same time. After three hours, P was closed, and Q and R filled the remaining tank in two hours. How many hours will P alone take to fill the tank?
questions.solution:
Part of the tank filled per hour by P + Q + R = 1/4

Part of the tank filled per hour by Q + R = 1/8

P + Q + R = 1/4 ⇒ 3(P + Q + R) + 2(Q + R) = 1 ⇒ 3/4 + 2(Q + R) = 1

2(Q + R) = 1 - 3/4 = 1/4 ⇒ Q + R = 1/8

P = 1/4 - 1/8 = 1/8 ⇒ P alone : 1/(1/8) = 8 hours.
